results.corrected_extracted: The abstract describes the amount odds ratios as fold reductions in the amount of drugs used (four-fold overall, OR 4.37); they are proportional-odds ratios from a cumulative-logit model (Table 4, note [2]), the common odds of reporting a smaller rather than a larger amount at both cut-points (less or none against same or more; less, none or same against more), not measured reductions. The authors state that results and behaviours were self-reported, that false-positive and false-negative results were not examined and it is unknown whether negatives reflected improper use, and that the design supports associations, not causal conclusions.
results.note: Table 4 note [2]: cumulative-logit proportional-odds model, so the ratio holds at both cut-points (implied 4.20 and 4.32); most of the absolute contrast is fewer reports of using more (6 against 23 in 100). Improper use: 'unknown'.
